text:
maria: heads up — eval run for quantized-ggml-3b returned NaN for BERTScore and empty ROUGE outputs on the new harness run. looked like CI passed earlier, but nightly eval flagged it.
kevin: can you paste the runner logs? curious if it's a metric impl issue or an encoder returning zeros.
maria: paste: ```
 INFO runner: loading model quantized-ggml-3b
 INFO runner: running eval on 1200 samples
 INFO metrics: bertscore = nan
 INFO metrics: rouge = {
   "rouge-1": {"f": 0.0, "p": 0.0, "r": 0.0}
 }
 Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "eval/runner.py", line 412, in compute_metrics
    scores = bertscore(cands, refs)
  File "eval/metrics/bertscore.py", line 78, in bertscore
    cos = (emb_c @ emb_r.T) / (norm_c * norm_r)
 RuntimeWarning: invalid value encountered in true_divide
```
sam: that RuntimeWarning suggests norm_r or norm_c == 0 for some vectors. we saw this with quantized embedding tables when `--approx` mode zeroed very small values.
julia: yep — I hit this last month. PR #452 changed post-quantize normalization order; for short inputs the L2 norm dropped below float eps and division produced NaN. quick check: in our current code we do `emb = emb / (emb.norm(dim=-1, keepdim=True) + 1e-12)` but quantized->dequant path sometimes yields exact zeros for certain tokens.
nana: tiny add — the bertscore implementation assumes float32. when embedding arrays come back as int8->int8-view numpy arrays the `.norm()` returns ints then coerces unexpectedly. we need an explicit cast: `emb = emb.astype(np.float32)` before norm.
kevin: good find. can we add a small unit test to CI that constructs an edge-case embedding (near-zero vector) and assert no NaNs after normalization?
sam: yes. also we should gate the metric runner so NaNs are reported as metric_health: "nan_detected" and fail the eval job, rather than continuing and emitting zeros to dashboards.
maria: agreed. also: dashboard mapping issue — some historical runs have metric name `bertscore` (lowercase) while new harness uses `BERTScore` (camel). that's why the chart disappeared for quant runs. kevin, can you update the ingestion layer to accept case-insensitive metric names?
kevin: on it. do we want to backfill? there's ~300 past runs that may be affected.
maria: please add a backfill script but mark optional. more urgent: unify pass@k definition. i discovered the harness outputs `pass_at_k` computed using the sample-without-replacement estimator (the k-hat formula) but the dashboard was showing naive top-k hit rate from a different pipeline. so the team is comparing apples to oranges.
sam: ugh. we need a config field written to results.json telling downstream which method used. propose: "pass_at_k_method": "sample_estimator" or "pass_at_k_method": "topk_exact" plus "seed" for sampling runs.
julia: agree. also add "num_samples" and the "k" list used. our eval reproducibility has been poor because seeds weren't captured, especially after quantization experiments where RNG affects sampling.
nana: small note: sampler in runner used `random.sample` which is not numpy RNG; test harness uses numpy's RNG elsewhere. unify to a single RNG source to ensure determinism across envs.
kevin: I'll change runner to use our platform rng util (seeded) and add `runner_seed` to results.json. will update dashboard ingestion to prefer `pass_at_k_method` when present.
maria: for the test suite: add `tests/eval/test_metrics_edgecases.py` with three short tests: (1) bertscore_no_nan_on_zero_like_embeddings, (2) pass_at_k_consistency_between_estimators, (3) rouge_truncation_returns_zero_not-null.
sam: for (2) we should include a small script to compute both estimators deterministically and assert difference < 1e-6 when identical assumptions are used. snippet:
```
# sample estimator (m,k,n)
# from https://arxiv.org/abs/1902.01838
def pass_at_k_sample_estimator(n, m, k):
    return 1 - comb(n - m, k) / comb(n, k)
``` 
(not exact code — will add proper implementation)
maria: eval-bot just flagged a CI run: `eval-bot: CI run 1790012400 failed: metrics_nan_detected — https://ci.internal/runs/1790012400` 
kevin: thanks for the ping. i'll prioritize the normalization/astype fix and the results.json metadata additions. will also add a lightweight backfill tool `tools/backfill_metric_case_insensitive.py` that re-ingests old results.
julia: PR up for the NaN guard + cast: https://git.internal/redwood/pull/487 — includes unit tests and a small harness change to emit `metric_health`.
maria: sweet. once merged please trigger nightly eval. also update the dashboard alert: fire when `metric_health` == `nan_detected` or when `pass_at_k_method` changes between runs for same model/version.
nana: noted. adding alert to ops runbook.
maria: thanks all. action items: kevin update ingestion + backfill (owner: kevin), sam add pass@k determinism test (owner: sam), julia merged PR and will monitor (owner: julia), ana update runbook (owner: ana). i'll follow up on the nightly run result tomorrow. :thumbsup:
kevin: on it.
sam: working on tests.
julia: monitoring.
nana: runbook updated, added links.
eval-bot: CI run 1790012467 started: nightly-eval/quantized (will post results).
maria: ok closing the thread for now, please DM me if something urgent crops up.
